main_text.p: & reliqua turba omnis (id est, calones & lixæ) concla-marunt. Et illi quidem hastas aut pila ad scuta concutie-bant, Calones tempore.{*}isti lapides etiam ad aera vasa: Quâ tamen nar-ratione hoc de calonibus nouum, & temporis illius modò fuit, nec trahendum ad morem: tunc scilicet vsur-patum, quò maior sonus strepitusque esset terrendo ho-sti. At de militibus ipsis, iterùm Dio in pugnâ Philip-pensi: καὶ[?] τότε ἀλαλάξαντες οἱ ὁπλῖται, τάς τε ἀσπίδας ὡς δοράτιοις[?] ἔκρουσαν[?], καὶ ἐκεῖνα ἐπ᾽ ἀλλήλας ἐξηκόντισαν: Deinde (post classicum) clamantes milites, scuta sua pilis percus-serunt, & eaipsa in sese mutuò iecerunt. Mansit mos Am-miani etiam æuo, atque ipse cum causâ addità prodit: Quibus occurrere bene pertinax miles explicatis ordinibus parans, hastisque feriens scuta (qui habitus iam pugnan-tium concitat & dolorem) proximo iam gestu terrebat. Quod ipsum vsurpabant etiam nondum vicino hostè, & cùm duci in eum vellent. Idem scriptor: Nec finiri perpessi quæ dicebantur, stridore dentium infrendentes, ar-dorémque pugnandi hastis illidendo scuta monstrantes. Et meminisse huic rei oportet, quæ dixi in Assensu mili-tari, suprà. Habes de clamore, qui tanti apud illos æsti-matus, ut ex eo diiudicarent de euentu pugnæ. Liuius: Clamor indicium primum fuit, quo res inclinatura esset. ex-citatior crebriorque ab hoste (Volsco) sublatus; ab Roma-nis dissonus, impar, segnis, sæpe iteratus, prodidit pauorem animorum. Simile Plutarchus in futura clade Crassiana. Cùm is, inquit, suos clamorem tollere iussisset; mæstitiam eorum accusauit, quod imbecillum, & inæqualem edidissent. Avd. Hoc mihi mirum: & tantine ea res? an homines, ut aues, olim clamore abigebantur? Lips. Ne illude.

page.notes: Printed marginal notes: "* Calones tempore." (left, beside the line with "isti"), "Lib. XLVII." (left), "Lib.xliii." (left, the numeral is doubtful), "Lib.xvi." (left), "Clamor momenta habebat. Lib.xiiii." (left, the last line is a reference). Only the first is marked with a reference mark in the text (*). The "Clamor" note is given as one note at the "Clamor indicium" line. The Greek reads uncertainly: the opening word, δοράτιοις and ἔκρουσαν are marked [?]. The long s is copied as s throughout. The paragraph breaks are hard to judge from the scan; the page is treated as one paragraph, which may merge printed paragraphs. The left-margin notes are not placed in exact mid-sentence positions, which may be imprecise. The catchword "momen-" is given as printed, with its hyphen.
